title: Unearned Flood Premium of a Withdrawn Term: Flat Cancellation and Duplicate Coverage
content:
For a flood insurance term that a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts paid and that was later withdrawn, the unearned flood premium is set as follows in two situations.

## Flat basis

Where the days in force — calendar days from the day the withdrawn term began to the cancellation date — are zero, the flat basis applies: the whole payment is unearned, because the term was cancelled before it began.

## Duplicate-coverage basis

Where the days in force are above zero and the cancellation date is the due date of a paid replacement flood bill (the latest paid flood insurance bill falls due on or after the day the withdrawn term began, and its due date is the cancellation date), the duplicate-coverage basis applies. The earned flood policy fee of 50.00 is first taken off the reserve's payment as fully earned, and the remainder is multiplied by the policy-year days, 365, less the days in force, and divided by 365.

Where the days in force are above zero and the cancellation date is not such a due date, this rule does not set the unearned premium.

## Input, judgement, output (hypothetical payments)

| Payment | Days in force | Cancellation date is a paid replacement bill's due date | Unearned flood premium |
|---|---|---|---|
| 965.00 | 0 | — | 965.00 |
| 965.00 | 73 | Yes | 965.00 less 50.00 is 915.00; times 292, divided by 365: 732.00 |
| 415.00 | 146 | Yes | 365.00 times 219, divided by 365: 219.00 |
| 965.00 | 73 | No | Not set by this rule |
